Smith's index of soil heterogeneity

Source: R/pathology.R
smith_index.Rd

From a uniformity trial (one crop, uniformly managed, harvested in small basic units) builds every plot shape that tiles the field exactly (length units along the rows times width units along the columns), computes for each the variance per unit area among plots, V_x = var(T / x) with T the plot totals and x the plot size in basic units, and fits Smith's empirical law V_x = V_1 / x^b by least squares on the log scale (weighted by the degrees of freedom of each variance, plots - 1, unless weights = "none").

Usage

smith_index(
  data,
  cost_ratio = NULL,
  weights = c("df", "none"),
  min_plots = 2,
  strips = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A numeric matrix (or data frame) of yields of the basic units, with the rows and columns of the field.

cost_ratio

Optional ratio of the cost per plot to the cost per unit area of experimental land (both per basic unit).

weights

"df" (default) or "none".

min_plots

Smallest number of plots a shape must give to enter the fit (at least 2).

strips

Use in the fit the shapes that span the whole length or width of the field. They are left out by default (as in agricolae): one strip per row or column averages out any gradient along it, so a few such shapes can dominate the fit, and they cannot be blocked.

Value

An object of class "ad_smith" with the table of shapes (table: size, width, length, plots, df, variance, cv, used), the index b, the fitted V1, the R squared of the log-log fit, the mean yield, the coefficient of variation of the basic units (cv1) and Smith's optimum plot size (optimum).

Details

The index b lies usually between 0 and 1. Near 1, adjacent units are nearly uncorrelated and larger plots reduce the variance per unit area efficiently; near 0, adjacent units are much alike and enlarging plots gains little, so more replicates pay off better. Given the ratio of the cost per plot to the cost per unit area (cost_ratio = K1 / K2), Smith's optimum plot size is b K1 / ((1 - b) K2) basic units; see hatheway_size() for the size needed to detect a given difference.

References

Smith, H. F. (1938). An empirical law describing heterogeneity in the yields of agricultural crops. Journal of Agricultural Science 28, 1-23.

Gomez, K. A. and Gomez, A. A. (1984). Statistical Procedures for Agricultural Research, 2nd ed. Wiley, New York, chapter 12.

Examples

sm <- smith_index(uniformity_trial, cost_ratio = 2)
sm
